title: LLM Ops sprint notes — caching, routing, quantization (personal scratchpad)
content:
Context: went to the LLM Ops sprint breakout (small workshop) on 2026-03-14 — this is a raw, personal capture of ideas, small sketches, and action items. Mostly to jog memory and surface experiments to try on Redwood Dedicated and Private sims. Not polished — lots of questions left open.

High-level takeaways (one-line):
- Caching wins depend heavily on request shape: short-chat vs long-document ingestion have almost orthogonal optima.
- Smart routing (by token budget + model variant) avoids expensive fallbacks but needs cheap per-request cost estimation.
- Quantization progress means 4-bit mix-precision is viable for many gen tasks but brittle on edge cases (rare tokens, numeracy).

Notes from sessions (rough):
1) Prefix/KV caching practicalities
- Paper notes: Efficient Prefix KV Caching (arXiv draft linked above) — key idea: hierarchical prefix index with eviction by recency + access frequency, store low-cost compressed caches for cold contexts.
- Implementation constraints for Redwood: cache keying must be stable across model variants and quantization states. That implies we store "semantic fingerprint" (hash of tokenizer-normalized prefix) + model-variant tag.
- Memory accounting: for 70B dense, warm KV per token ~ 1.6KB (made-up calc; need to re-measure). For quantized kernels (4-bit), KV memory halves? but access cost increases.
- Heuristic: only cache prefixes > 32 tokens and that appear >= 2x per hour for a customer. Test cutoff at 64 tokens.
- Edge case: user does iterative prompt editing (small edits to prefix) — naive exact-keying loses hits. Consider LSH or rolling-window hash to get approximate matches.

Quick pseudo-sketch (very rough):
- On request: compute prefix_hash = sha256(normalize(prefix))
- Lookup cache[prefix_hash, model_variant] -> kv_snapshot candidate
- If not found, compute LSH buckets for prefix, check nearest candidates for partial KV reuse (warm-start KVs)
- If candidate found "partial_hit": rehydrate with partial KV and fill remaining layers on first tokens streamed.

Questions:
- How to version KV layout across model checkpoints? If we change layer ordering / fused kernels, KVs might not be compatible. Need per-variant migration plan (recompute or fallback).
- How much does streaming latency suffer when rehydrating partial KV? Measure p50/p95 specifically for interactive 200ms SLO.

2) Routing by cost + latency
- Idea from breakout: attach a tiny estimator model to each incoming request that predicts token cost and latency (cheap classifier). Use that to route to: hosted-fast, dedicated, or cheap-quantized variant.
- Estimator features: prompt length (tokens), presence of code/markdown (higher compute per token), is_continuation (chat turn), historical per-customer avg token length.
- Quick experiment: train a logistic regressor on 100k historical requests (labels: high_cost_bucket / low_cost_bucket). Cheap, interpretable.
- Risk: estimator must not leak PII. Keep features token-count-level only.

3) Quantization observations and gotchas
- Hands-on demo: HF microbench on 4-bit QAT for LLaMA2-Chat 70B gave ~1.9x token throughput vs 8-bit but saw a 3–5% drop in ROUGE for summarization datasets. Note: not uniform across tasks.
- Strange failure mode: numeracy tests (dates, arithmetic) became flaky after aggressive quant. Suspect rounding in layernorm/softmax accumulation precision.
- Practical rule: for production-critical paths (billing/invoice summarization, code generation), keep at least 8-bit or mixed (8-bit attention + 4-bit MLP).

Actionable experiments to run (labelled with priority):
- EXP-1 (P0): KV-cache cutoff sweep. Measure cost savings and cold-miss latencies with cutoffs at 16/32/64/128 tokens. Run on replayed traffic (sanitized) for 7 days. Track: token cost, p50/p95 latency, hit rate. Linked Jira: INF-482.
- EXP-2 (P1): LSH-based approximate prefix matching. Prototype a tiny LSH index using MinHash on sub-token shingles; measure false positive/neg rates on user-edit traces.
- EXP-3 (P1): Training tiny routing estimator. Dataset: 200k labeled requests (internal), train logistic + small CART. Evaluate on separate 20k. Metrics: precision@top1 for high-cost routing.
- EXP-4 (P2): Quantization AB test. Deploy on dedicated pool only (no customer-facing change), split traffic 90/10. Tasks: summarization, codegen, Q/A. Monitor output-quality regressions and regress alerts from Redwood Optimize.

Personal ideas & scribbles (brainstorm):
- "Graceful degradation" pattern: if dedicated capacity saturating, route to quantized model + notify app with a "quality hint" header. Apps can opt-in to degrade or require fallback correctness.
- Caching policy with TTL tiers: hot (minutes), warm (hours), cold (days). Cold entries compressed (FP16->8-bit compress) but require re-expand cost.
- Cost-prediction shim in SDK: expose expected_token_cost_estimate in response headers so customers can proactively alter generation. Good for PLG transparency.

References that I should read more carefully:
- Efficient Prefix KV Caching (arXiv link in linked_artifacts) — high priority to read whole thing.
- HF blog: "Practical 4-bit Quantization for Large Transformers" (search, 2025) — notes from demo at workshop.
- 2025 NeurIPS paper on "Approximate Context Reuse" (need to fetch PDF).

Open questions / followups for team sync:
- @Maya: can we export 7d of sanitized prefix hit/miss telemetry for EXP-1? (Maya said she'd check)
- @Evan: can infra allocate a small dedicated pool for P0 experiments (nightly runs)?
- Need SRE buy-in for partial-KV rehydrates — potential increased IOPS at fill time.

To-dos (short):
- [ ] Draft EXP-1 plan and attach cost estimate + infra needs (deadline: 2026-03-21).
- [ ] Pull historical request sample (100k) for routing estimator dataset (deadline: 2026-03-20).
- [ ] Sync with Maya + Owen on KV keying migration plan (meeting: next Tue).

Quick note to self about writing up for Confluence: keep this doc as a raw capture, then synth into a one-pager for eng-ops and a separate short doc for product describing "what customers will see" under graceful degradation.

Tiny rough log of conversation snippets I liked: "cache smarter not bigger" (Evan) and "route by expected cost not just latency" (Maya).

End of notes.
